requests.filedBy: NEW3 (raised on RCC's behalf while verifying CCR-01)
requests.endpoint: POST /search — `retrievalOutcome.rarestDf` and the 'Known v1 limits' section
requests.missing: Two statements in the frozen contract are now false, and one field's meaning was never stated. (a) The contract says 'A party name alone returns zero'. Measured 30 Aug: 'SATENDER KUMAR ANTIL' returns 3 results with the authority at rank 1 in 295.6 ms. (b) The contract says 'a broad term inside a narrow filter is still refused'. Measured: 'bail' restricted to one named court over one month returns 5 results in 418.1 ms, and over three days 5 results in 154.6 ms. (c) `rarestDf` is documented only as 'number, present whether or not it refused'. Measured across six scopes of the same query it is INVARIANT at 0.25773984261292154 — identical in the scopes that refuse AND in the two that succeed. It is a corpus-wide document frequency and is not the bound that governed the decision.
requests.rccFallback: RCC currently builds refusal screens against a stated limit that no longer holds, and could reasonably read `rarestDf` as scoped to the query's filters. Neither has shipped, so nothing user-facing is wrong today.
requests.affectedSurface: search results, the refusal/empty state, and any future narrowing hint derived from rarestDf
requests.userTruthImpact: If RCC renders or reasons from `rarestDf` as a scoped number, a user who has already narrowed to one court and one month can be told their query is too broad on the strength of a corpus-wide statistic. That is the daily-loop case and the one where narrowing is exactly what they did.
requests.schemaDelta: NONE. No field is added, removed, renamed or retyped. `contract` stays 1.
requests.semanticDelta: `retrievalOutcome.rarestDf` is defined as the CORPUS-WIDE document frequency of the query's rarest lexeme. It is invariant under `filters` and it is NOT the bound that admitted or refused this request. RCC may show it to a developer and may not derive a user-facing narrowing hint from it. The two 'Known v1 limits' bullets are superseded by the measured states in V1_CAPABILITY_REGISTRY_R13.json.

requests.filedVia: NEW3 R13, Gate-B per-platform capability audit
requests.missing: A platform dimension. Observed 30 Aug: the response is `{registryVersion, asOf, capabilities}` where `capabilities` is a flat map of 24 rows, each `{state, reason, asOf, unblockedBy}`. The string 'platform' does not appear anywhere in the payload. Roadmap v7.1 §9.5 requires party-name search to be disableable on iOS WITHOUT disabling exact case / CNR / citation / case-number research, and §3 rule 15 forbids any claim on a surface the registry does not mark ENABLED **per platform**.
requests.rccFallback: RCC can hard-code a build-time platform flag. That works and is what v1 will ship if this is not amended — but it means turning party search off on iOS requires an App Store release, which is precisely the situation the kill switch exists to avoid.
requests.affectedSurface: search input and its results on iOS; the App Store listing, transitively
requests.userTruthImpact: If App Review objects to party-name search under guideline 5.1.1(viii), a build-time flag means the capability stays live until a new binary is approved. A served flag makes it a same-day change. Separately: a capability disabled on iOS while the listing claims it is a per-platform claim defect.
requests.schemaDelta: ADDITIVE. Each row in `capabilities` gains an OPTIONAL `platforms` object: `{ios: State, android: State, web: State}` where State is the existing four-state vocabulary (ENABLED | LIMITED | DISABLED | EXPERIMENTAL_INTERNAL). A row with no `platforms` key means all platforms take the row's top-level `state` — so every existing client keeps working unchanged and `contract` stays 1.
requests.semanticDelta: Where `platforms` is present it is authoritative FOR THAT PLATFORM and the top-level `state` is the union/marketing-neutral summary. A client reads its own platform's entry and falls back to `state`. Disabling `search.party_name_only` on iOS MUST NOT change the state of `search.exact_citation`, `search.cnr`, `search.case_number` or `search.case_title_full` — those are separate rows and are separately served.
requests.capabilityImpact: Makes the iOS party-search kill switch representable on the wire. Enables nothing by itself.
requests.claimImpact: Prerequisite for the per-platform claims register being enforceable at runtime rather than only at review time.
requests.releaseBlockedBy: No backend serves `platforms` yet. RCC MUST NOT build against it. Until it lands, the iOS kill switch is a build-time flag and the degrade behaviour in V1_CAPABILITY_REGISTRY_R13.json is what RCC implements.
requests.handoff: LCC — additive field on an existing route, no migration, no new endpoint.

requests.filedVia: NEW3 R13, trust-state product contract review
requests.missing: `treatment_provenance` on the wire. The claims register records B4 as BLOCKED on exactly this: migration 0082's own comment says 'Nothing reads this column yet', and a reporter's headnote and a court's own words currently render identically.
requests.rccFallback: RCC renders one undifferentiated LAW MOVED state. Nothing false is stated — the amber mark means the law has moved and that is true in both cases — but the advocate cannot see whether a court or a law reporter said so.
requests.affectedSurface: judgment reader, saved authority in a matter
requests.userTruthImpact: 99 of 104 LAW MOVED states rest on a reporter's editorial annotation and 5 on a court's own words (NEW2 bus 1145). Rendering them identically lets an advocate believe a court has spoken when a reporter has. It does not make anything shown FALSE, which is why this is P1 and not P0.
requests.rationale: The wire field is LCC Sprint-2/3 work and is on the named-gaps table as the trust-state contract row. RCC does not need it to ship the reader. Deferring is safe ONLY because the interim copy is already constrained: claims register B2c blocks the words 'set aside' entirely and B3 forbids naming a court as the source of a reporter's annotation.
requests.interimBehaviour: One LAW MOVED state, no source attribution shown, and the reporter-class copy from claims register B3 used wherever a source is implied: 'A law report records this as overruled. We have not confirmed this against the deciding court.'
